QUOTE: Only translation units that define `MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` before the first include of `private_access.h` see the real names. ... The default is the external user. ... Public headers declare struct members as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)`, so the member is really named `private_state`. A user writing `ssl->state` gets a compile error.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that code defining the opt-out macro sees the real plain names, while ordinary external consumers see the `private_`-prefixed names.
